rules.rule: If an image shows distant objects, their darkest values must be lighter than the foreground's darkest value; true blacks in the distance indicate no atmospheric perspective.
rules.evidence: Blacks stop being black. Nothing in the far distance is as dark as the darkest thing in the foreground.

rules.rule: If an image uses a uniform grey wash over the entire frame without increasing with distance, it fails to demonstrate atmospheric perspective.
rules.evidence: Only if it increases with distance. A uniform grey wash over the frame is just a washed-out picture.
